abstract: How does the brain give rise to human capabilities like language processing or logical reasoning? This question has captured the minds of many cognitive scientists and neuroscientists, and indeed has a history dating back at least as far as the philosophers of ancient Greece. Until recently, humans were the only systems that we knew of that showed these capacities across broad domains. But after recent developments in the field of artificial intelligence, language models have begun to show some surprising parallels to complex cognitive capacities and the neural representations that underpin them - despite the architectures and learning paradigms of these models differing dramatically from biological systems. In this primer, I will provide a brief overview of language models, their construction and training, and the phenomena of natural intelligence that they might help us to understand. First, let us begin with a bit of history.
